reaction: The distinction between muscle-forming cells and fused mature fibres is useful.

mostWorthwhile.text: Building living supporting tissue from fibroblasts and their extracellular matrix was most worthwhile: it showed that tissue includes both cells and material they produce around themselves.

leastWorthwhile.text: The final muscle-branch combination repeated the RNA-to-protein pattern already shown for fibroblasts, though the distinction from mature fibres added value.

surprise.text: The supporting tissue required extracellular processing and assembly after the cells made procollagen, rather than simply producing finished collagen fibres inside the cells.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, though combining the fibroblasts with the matrix they had just produced felt somewhat redundant. The resulting picture clarified that both were part of the tissue.

continue.text: I would continue: the unfinished development of the myoblasts gives me a reason to see how muscle fibres form. I would also hope for explanations of terms such as paraxial mesoderm, procollagen and ground substance.
